mcqs.question: A large drum is struck hard and produces a sound that can be heard from a great distance, while a small hand‑clap produces a faint sound. Which statement best defines the property of the sound that is responsible for this difference?

options.A: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles in the medium from their rest position.
options.B: Amplitude is the number of vibrations per second of the source.
options.C: Amplitude is the time taken for one complete vibration.
options.D: Amplitude is the speed at which the sound wave travels through air.

mcqs.answer: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles in the medium from their rest position.
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude measures how far particles in the medium move from their equilibrium position during a vibration. A larger amplitude means greater energy transfer, producing a louder sound. Option B describes frequency, C describes time period, and D describes speed of sound, which are different concepts.

mcqs.question: A student notices that a piano key produces a higher‑pitched note than a bass guitar string when both are plucked. In the given scenario, which definition correctly explains the property that determines this difference?

options.A: Frequency is the number of complete vibrations made by the source in one second.
options.B: Frequency is the maximum distance the particles move from their rest position.
options.C: Frequency is the time taken for one complete vibration of the source.
options.D: Frequency is the speed at which the sound wave travels through the medium.

mcqs.answer: Frequency is the number of complete vibrations made by the source in one second.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency, measured in hertz (Hz), tells how many cycles occur each second and directly influences pitch – higher frequency gives higher pitch. Option B defines amplitude, C defines time period (inverse of frequency), and D defines speed of sound.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the time period of a sound wave is correct?

options.A: The time period is the duration of one complete vibration of the source.
options.B: The time period is the number of vibrations occurring each second.
options.C: The time period is the same as the amplitude of the wave.
options.D: The time period is the speed at which the wave travels through air.

mcqs.answer: The time period is the duration of one complete vibration of the source.
mcqs.explanation: Time period (T) is the time taken for one full cycle, measured in seconds. It is the reciprocal of frequency (f = 1/T). Option B describes frequency, C confuses with amplitude, and D describes wave speed.

mcqs.question: If the frequency of a tuning fork is doubled, what happens to its time period?

options.A: The time period becomes half of its original value.
options.D: The time period becomes four times larger.

mcqs.answer: The time period becomes half of its original value.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency (f) and time period (T) are inversely related: f = 1/T. Doubling f means T = 1/f becomes half of its previous value. Options B, C, and D ignore the inverse relationship.

mcqs.question: Two identical speakers emit pure tones of the same frequency. Speaker A vibrates with an amplitude of 2 mm, while Speaker B vibrates with an amplitude of 0.5 mm. Which statement correctly compares the loudness of the sounds produced?

options.A: Speaker A produces a sound that is louder than Speaker B because larger amplitude transfers more energy to the air.
options.B: Speaker A and Speaker B produce sounds of equal loudness because they have the same frequency.
options.C: Speaker B is louder because a smaller amplitude results in a higher pitch.
options.D: Speaker B is louder because lower amplitude reduces the speed of the sound wave.

mcqs.answer: Speaker A produces a sound that is louder than Speaker B because larger amplitude transfers more energy to the air.
mcqs.explanation: Loudness is directly related to the amplitude of the sound wave; greater amplitude means more energy and a louder perception. Frequency determines pitch, not loudness (eliminating B). Options C and D incorrectly link amplitude to pitch or speed.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, a question states: "A sound wave of 500 Hz is heard as a low note, while a sound wave of 2000 Hz is heard as a high note. Which of the following best explains this observation?"

options.A: Higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch, so the 2000 Hz wave is heard as a higher note.
options.B: Higher frequency corresponds to greater amplitude, making the note sound higher.
options.C: Higher frequency shortens the time period, which directly raises the pitch.
options.D: Higher frequency increases the speed of sound, causing a higher pitch.

mcqs.answer: Higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch, so the 2000 Hz wave is heard as a higher note.
mcqs.explanation: Pitch is the perceptual attribute of sound that depends primarily on frequency; a larger number of vibrations per second (higher frequency) is perceived as a higher pitch. Option B confuses amplitude with pitch, C mentions time period correctly but the direct cause of pitch is frequency, not the period itself, and D incorrectly links frequency to speed of sound (speed is independent of frequency in a given medium).

mcqs.question: What is the definition of amplitude in a sound wave?

options.A: The maximum displacement of particles of the medium from their equilibrium position.
options.B: The number of vibrations per second made by the source.
options.C: The time taken for one complete vibration of the source.
options.D: The speed at which the sound wave travels through the medium.

mcqs.answer: The maximum displacement of particles of the medium from their equilibrium position.
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude measures how far particles move from rest during a vibration; it determines the loudness of the sound. Options B, C, and D describe frequency, time period, and wave speed respectively.

mcqs.question: Frequency of a sound wave is best described as:

options.A: The number of complete vibrations that occur in one second.
options.B: The maximum distance particles move from their rest position.
options.C: The time required for one complete vibration.
options.D: The speed of the sound wave in air.

mcqs.answer: The number of complete vibrations that occur in one second.
mcqs.explanation: Frequency, measured in hertz (Hz), counts how many cycles happen each second and determines the pitch of the sound. Option B defines amplitude, C defines time period, and D defines wave speed.
